findings.detail: Kernel, nvidia-smi, and 11 inspected CUDA/NVML/GLX/EGL/OptiX/RTX compiler/rendering libraries agree on 610.43.02; /opt/nvidia-drivers does not exist. This is not a claim about every library mapped by the terminated process.

A0 sets CVD to GPU4 UUID and renderer activeGpu=4. Kit logs explicit CVD enumeration/crash warning and 14 CUDA-bad-state GPU skips, but Vulkan table still marks physical GPU4 active. Therefore simple wrong-Vulkan-GPU selection is not shown, and interop trouble remains plausible.

findings.finding: A0 reaches Kit startup, then crashes during stage creation/viewport Hydra enable
findings.detail: Exit -11 occurs after kit_startup_returned, in context.new_stage() callback. A0 did not reach RGB-frame validation. Python traceback alone does not identify the crashing native plugin/instruction.

findings.finding: Packaged RTX scenedb duplicates match exactly
Standalone ldd is not equivalent to Kit process loading
findings.detail: Direct A0-loader-path ldd on RTX/Hydra misses dependencies; every listed name exists in the installed runtime. Kit extension configs have native libraries/plugin dependency paths. No claim that these were absent in A0 is justified by isolated ldd.

findings.finding: All GPUs idle at audit snapshot
findings.detail: All eight GPUs show 1MiB/0% and compute-process query is empty. No workloads were stopped by this audit; earlier A0 snapshot is a different time.

findings.finding: Custom minimal Kit bootstrap remains an independent configuration variable
findings.detail: A0 used a0_camera.kit/KitApp and logs missing isaacsim.simulation_app extension path warnings. Without comparison to validated stock SimulationApp startup, native driver incompatibility is not established.

findings.finding: Unmasked CUDA ordinal4 matches Vulkan physicalGPU4
findings.detail: With CVD absent and CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID, cuInit and all device identity calls return0; ordinal4 is PCI0000:81:00.0 and UUIDGPU-e1a460e9-e272-b227-222e-0dbb77c248c5. No CUDA contexts/kernels were created.

limitations: No simulator, CUDA context/kernel, Vulkan instance, or camera was launched by this audit. An explicitly authorized CUDA Driver API inventory called cuInit and device identity queries only.
No native core dump/loaded-map trace from A0 was available; actual dlopen resolutions and faulting native stack remain unknown.
Driver compatibility for this exact Isaac Sim 5.1/610.43.02 combination is not established by matching library filenames.
Multiple packaged Vulkan loaders exist, but filesystem duplication alone is not evidence they were concurrently loaded.
These findings cover archived A0 and static state at recorded_at_utc; later root-owned A1 experiments are separate evidence.
next_diagnostic_hypotheses: Under root-owned authorized experiments, separate CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES interop/enumeration from renderer GPU selection and verify physical GPU UUID independently.
Compare validated stock SimulationApp startup against custom minimal Kit bootstrap before attributing failure to host driver.
Collect loaded-library mappings and a native stack if the reproducible crash persists; preserve one-variable-at-a-time evidence.
